safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 2.09 days

narrative: Material PL1__M1E26DD7 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=29.9%) with a mild decreasing trend over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=39.4%), and lead-time variance contributes 83.7% of total demand-during-lead-time uncertainty, making supplier reliability the dominant risk factor. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with safety stock of 20,959 units and order quantity of 55,455 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level target while respecting the storage capacity constraint of 94,088 units.
warnings: SAP safety stock is currently 0 — provides no buffer for a material with 39.4% lead-time CV
Lead time variability is dominant (83.7% of variance) — supplier reliability improvement recommended
SAP safety lead time (3.0 days) is slightly over-conservative vs data-driven recommendation (2.09 days)

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous and non-zero every working day with moderate variability (CV~30%). The (r,Q) model is optimal for materials with stable positive demand where a fixed order quantity minimises total ordering and holding costs; EOQ provides the cost-minimising Q while z-score safety stock ensures the 95% service level against combined demand and lead-time uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (76,414 units post-replenishment vs 94,088 limit), providing 18% headroom. If safety stock or order quantity were to increase materially, the capacity constraint could become active.
